title: Adaptive RBAC telemetry & pen-test remediation: action plan for auth drift, admin controls, and SAML auditability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket consolidates the remediation work from the recent third-party penetration test and our internal threat model for RBAC v2, SSO/SAML integration, and admin controls. Objective is to deliver an actionable engineering plan: implement telemetry for authorization decisions, surface admin-role changes in immutable audit events, harden SAML assertion validation, and deploy a short-lived break-glass flow with approvals.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- Telemetry pipeline additions: emit a standardized 'authorization_decision' audit event for every call that evaluates a policy (fields: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, resource, action, decision, policy_version, request_id, evaluation_latency, saml_assertion_hash?). Events must be immutable and propagated to the centralized audit pipeline (BigQuery + long-term cold storage).
- RBAC drift detection: nightly job that compares live principal bindings against canonical source-of-truth (RBAC store) and opens automated Drift tickets for deviations.
- Admin-change alerting: create high-severity alert when scoped admin roles are granted or escalate beyond configured thresholds (notify PagerDuty + Console banner).
- SAML hardening: validate assertion audience and issuer strictly, enforce signature and certificate rotation checks, fingerprint SAML assertions for audit linkage. Add tests for malformed/duplicate assertions discovered during pen-test.
- Break-glass / JIT admin flow: implement time-limited elevated token issuance via authenticated console flow with approval audit trail and auto-revocation.
- E2E regression tests: run an internal red-team scenario and add automated CI tests to prevent regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Authorization_decision events emitted for >= 95% of production API calls (non-proxy paths accounted for) and landed in audit BigQuery table with schema validated by SEC.
2) Admin-role changes generate immutable audit events and a PagerDuty alert within 60s for P0 escalations.
3) SAML assertion failures exploited in pen-test are closed or mitigated; SAML test suite added to CI.
4) Break-glass flow is available in staging with UI, approval log, and auto-revocation; internal red-team reproduces successful JIT lifecycle.
5) Documentation updated: Confluence threat model, runbook for incident, and SOC2 evidence checklist completed.

Background and rationale:
The recent external penetration test surfaced two categories of findings: authorization decision telemetry gaps (missing audit linkage between SSO assertions and RBAC decisions) and weak signals around admin privilege grants (no short-lived path or approval record). During threat modeling we identified two realistic attack chains where an attacker could escalate by combining a stale service-account binding with an unmonitored admin grant. This ticket bundles remediation work to close that chain and add observable guardrails.

Implementation notes / design decisions to consider:
- Event format: use existing audit event envelope; add 'authorization_decision' type and a policy_version tag. Keep payload small to avoid high QPS cost but include a truncated saml_assertion_hash to link back to raw SAML logs retained in cold storage.
- Storage: stream into current audit ingestion (LogRouter -> BigQuery streaming table) with downstream job to compress into cold GCS monthly. Retention policy to satisfy compliance: 7 years for admin-change events.
- Drift detection: leverage snapshot diffs of RBAC datastore (weekly) and compare with live bindings from Identity provider SCIM; create actionable tickets with exact diff and suggested rollback.
- Break-glass: prefer issuing a scoped short-lived JWT minted by auth-service that includes 'elevated_until' and 'approval_id'; approval stored immutably. UI shows who approved, reason, and auto-expiry.
- SAML: add certificate fingerprint rotation detection in SAMLAudit service, reject assertions signed by expired certs, and add SAML fuzzing tests discovered during pen-test.

Artifacts & references:
- Pen-test report (redacted): drive.google.com/drive/fake/pen-test-2026-rbac.pdf
- Threat model doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Threat+Model
- Audit schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1420
- RBAC drift prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz/pull/398
- Break-glass UI mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/break-glass-mock.jpg

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (this ticket): unblock infra for streaming new event type and land schema migration (observability team, PR #1420).
- Week 2: implement decision emission in authz service behind a feature flag; land SAML assertion validation fixes in saml-provider.
- Week 3: enable break-glass prototype in staging and run internal red-team.
- Week 4: production rollout to a subset of customers (internal + 5 pilot teams) with high-sensitivity monitoring; run compliance evidence collection.

Risks / open questions:
- QPS cost of emitting events for every authorization decision — need to cap or sample non-admin low-risk paths to control cost.
- Linking SAML assertions to API requests reliably when requests are proxied through several internal components. Proposal: propagate request_id and saml_assertion_hash in trace headers.
- Org change management: some teams rely on long-lived admin bindings; migration will require a communications plan and a temporary opt-out.

Next steps (immediate):
- [ ] Kick-off with Observability team to finalize event schema (owner: @marcus).
- [ ] Security to run the SAML fuzzing harness and share failing test cases (owner: @aisha).
- [ ] Schedule red-team for Week 3 and identify scope.

Estimated work breakdown (rough):
- Observability schema + ingestion changes: 2 engineer-weeks
- AuthZ decision emission + tests: 2 engineer-weeks
- SAML hardening & tests: 2 engineer-weeks
- Break-glass UI + approval workflow + auto-revoke: 3 engineer-weeks (phased rollout)
- Drift detection job & ticketing: 1 engineer-week
